info.name: Muse Ember
info.description: Muse Ember is the smallest and most efficient reasoning model from Meta, built for the work agents repeat all day: tool calls, coding-agent subtasks and routing. It accepts text, images, video, audio, and PDF documents and returns text.

info.name: Hy4
info.description: Hy4 is the official release of Tencent’s Hy4 model, succeeding Hy4 preview with stronger agentic capabilities and better performance on long-horizon, real-world productivity tasks. It accepts text and image input, has a 1M-token context window and configurable reasoning effort.

info.name: Crouton Alpha
info.description: Crouton Alpha is an anonymous lightweight model built for scalable coding, agentic and multimodal workflows such as agentic sub-tasks, tool use and document analysis. It always reasons, with adjustable reasoning effort, over a 1M-token context, and is served anonymously from a stealth preview slot, free while cloaked.

info.name: GPT-6.1 Terra
info.description: Fast, efficient GPT-6.1 model from OpenAI for visual reasoning, computer use and natural writing, with text and image input over a 1.05M-token context. Tool calling uses the Responses API.

info.name: GPT-6.1 Terra
info.description: Fast, efficient GPT-6.1 model from OpenAI for visual reasoning, computer use and natural writing, with text and image input over a 1.05M-token context. Tool calling uses the Responses API.

info.name: GPT-6.1 Terra Pro
info.description: GPT-6.1 Terra served in pro reasoning mode for higher-quality answers on complex tasks, with text, image and file input over a 1.05M-token context. Pro mode spends far more reasoning tokens per request.

info.name: Kimi K3.1 Pro
info.description: Kimi K3.1 Pro is a multimodal reasoning model from Moonshot AI for coding, research, and agentic tool use, with a 1M-token context window.

info.name: Kimi K3.1 Pro Highspeed
info.description: High-speed variant of Kimi K3.1 Pro from Moonshot AI, with multimodal reasoning, agentic tool use, and a 1M-token context window.

info.name: MiniMax M3.1 Flash
info.description: MiniMax M3.1 Flash is MiniMax's fast, low-cost M-series reasoning model with a 1M-token context window. It accepts text, image and video input, always reasons (reasoning_effort low to max, max by default), and is built for coding, multi-step agent workflows and visual understanding.

info.name: Glimpse
info.description: Glimpse is a multimodal visual reasoning model from Elorian, built for visual understanding and complex visual reasoning in the physical world. It reasons directly over images and video, accepts text, image and video input and returns text.

info.name: Ternary Bonsai 2 9B
info.description: Ternary Bonsai 2 9B is a compact open-weight model from PrismML built on Qwen3.5, with ternary weights packed into 2 bits. It handles conversation, reasoning, tool calling and image understanding over a 262K-token context. Reasoning is on by default.

info.name: Beam 1.0 501B A23B
info.description: Beam 1.0 is Reflection's open-weight reasoning model for coding and long-horizon agentic workflows. A sparse mixture-of-experts with 501B total and 23B active parameters per token, it always reasons before answering, supports tool calling and structured outputs, and works over a 1M-token context.

info.name: Muse Spark Open
info.description: Muse Spark Open is a coding-optimized open-weight model from Meta, trained for agentic coding workflows with reliable tool calling and deep codebase understanding. It accepts text, images, video, audio, and PDF documents and returns text.

info.name: Moondream 3 Preview
info.description: Moondream 3 Preview is a vision-language model from Moondream with 9B total parameters and 2B active (mixture-of-experts). It handles visual question answering, captioning, OCR and visual reasoning over images, accepts text and image input and returns text.

info.name: Moondream 3.1
info.description: Moondream 3.1 is a vision-language model from Moondream, the successor to Moondream 3 Preview, with 9B total parameters and 2B active (mixture-of-experts). It handles visual question answering, captioning, OCR and visual reasoning over images, accepts text and image input and returns text.

info.name: Nemotron 3.5 Super VL
info.description: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Super VL is an open multimodal mixture-of-experts model with 12B active parameters out of 120B total. It takes text, images, documents, GUI screenshots and video as input and answers in text, with optional reasoning, tool calling and structured outputs.

info.name: Pareto 26.10
info.description: Pareto is a multimodal composite model built for research, coding, and agentic workflows, while delivering frontier-level performance across a broad range of general-purpose tasks.

info.name: Gemini 4 Argon
info.description: Gemini 4 Argon is Google’s flagship reasoning model, built for complex software engineering, deep mathematical and scientific problem solving, and autonomous multi-step agents.

info.name: LFM2.5-24B-A2B
info.description: LFM2.5-24B-A2B is a mixture-of-experts reasoning model from Liquid AI with 24B total and 2.45B active parameters. It always reasons before answering and is built for agents that call tools.

info.name: Summarize
info.description: Summarize is an abstractive summarization model from ScaleDown. It condenses long text and documents into a fluent, faithful rewrite rather than lifting sentences from the source, over a 1M-token context, and accepts text, image and file input. Its only tunable parameter is the output cap.

info.name: Muse Wonder
info.description: Muse Wonder is a frontier reasoning model from Meta, designed for complex personal and professional agentic tasks. It accepts text, images, video, audio, and PDF documents and returns text.

info.name: Step 5 Preview
info.description: Step 5 Preview is StepFun's flagship model for agentic work, built on a sparse Mixture-of-Experts architecture (27B active / 600B total parameters). It accepts text, image, and video input, always reasons (low / medium / high effort), supports a 1M-token context window, and performs strongly in software engineering and professional tasks.

info.name: Dynamic Router
info.description: A router you configure in the request. Describe up to ten buckets in your own words (`when`), each with the models to try in order, and name the decision model: it picks the bucket whose description fits each request — its text and its images — and the first model of that bucket that can take the request answers, falling back to the next one in your order. One `router` serves chat completions, the Responses API (`/v1/responses`), the Messages API (`/v1/messages`), image generation and editing, and video generation: list models of every kind in a bucket, and each request takes those of its own kind — on Responses and Messages, the models served there. A bucket with no models (`models: []`) ends the request at the decision: no model is called, the answer is empty (an empty message, no images, a video generation with no video), and `meta.router` gives your code the bucket to act on (`routed: false`) — only the judgement is charged. One bucket makes a plain fallback chain, with no judgement. Without a `router` object it routes a conversation like the Jev Router — light: GPT-6 Luna, Claude Haiku 5.5, DeepSeek V4.1 Flash, Gemini Flash-Lite; standard: GPT-6.1 Sol, Claude Sonnet 5.5; heavy: Claude Opus 5.5, GPT-6 Astra; on Responses and Messages, those of them served there — and a `router` that leaves a setting out keeps its default; image and video requests need buckets of your own. You pay the rate of the model that answers, named in `meta.model`, plus the judgement: one decision at its catalogue price, its images included, listed as its own request in your usage. `meta.router` says which bucket the request landed in, why, what the decision model chose and how sure it was, and how many images it was shown.

info.name: d1 Router
info.description: Routes each request to a model picked for it: Liquid AI d1 picks the bucket whose description fits the request — its text and its images — and the request goes to the first model of that bucket that can take it, falling back to the next one if it fails. Without a `router` object it routes a conversation — chat completions, the Responses API, the Messages API — by the default buckets — light (little capability needed: small talk, lookups, short routine tasks): GPT-6 Luna, Claude Haiku 5.5, DeepSeek V4.1 Flash, Gemini Flash-Lite; standard (multi-step tasks that need care): GPT-6.1 Sol, Claude Sonnet 5.5; heavy (complex reasoning, hard math, tricky code, expert knowledge): Claude Opus 5.5, GPT-6 Astra; on Responses and Messages, those of them served there. Light models do not reason unless you ask (`reasoning_effort`); standard and heavy ones may think before they answer. It is `aimlapi/dynamic-router` with `decision_model: liquid/d1`, and takes the same `router` object: up to ten buckets of your own, each described in your words (`when`) with the models to try in order, for chat completions, the Responses and Messages APIs, image generation and editing, and video generation — a bucket with no models (`models: []`) ends the request at the decision, with an empty answer — and `default_bucket`, `min_confidence` and `force_bucket`; only the decision model stays Liquid AI d1. You pay the rate of the model that answers, named in `meta.model` (and the `x-aimlapi-model` header when not streaming), plus the judgement: one `liquid/d1` decision at its catalogue price, its images included, listed as its own request in your usage (a turn that returns tool results goes back to the model that made the calls and needs none). `meta.router` says which bucket the request landed in, why, and how sure Liquid AI d1 was.

It is optimized for complex, multi-step reasoning, coding, and agentic workflows, with orchestration tokens billed as standard input/output tokens.
